lineage.strategy: Move from channel-partnership language to disclosed long-duration contracted infrastructure economics.

observations.fact: Nebius disclosed a five-year agreement to provide Meta $12 billion of dedicated capacity across multiple locations beginning in early 2027, based on large-scale NVIDIA Vera Rubin deployments.

Meta also committed to purchase remaining available compute across certain upcoming Nebius clusters up to $15 billion over five years after Nebius offers capacity to third-party cloud customers, bringing disclosed potential contract value to about $27 billion.

risks.risk: Large contracted capacity requires substantial buildout and execution; headline contract value is not equivalent to near-term revenue, free cash flow or margin.

unknowns.unknown: Site-level capex, financing costs, delivery milestones, gross margin and realized utilization economics are not disclosed in the announcement.

recommendation: Use the disclosed duration and capacity commitments as strong source-addressed demand evidence while separately underwriting financing, deployment and margin realization.
